top_choice_rationale: P001 awards the original, experimentally verified invention of the optical lattice clock: trapping many neutral atoms at a magic wavelength so the lattice does not shift the clock transition. The 10^-18 performance is reproduced by independent laboratories, so maturity is not in doubt, and the citation can rest on the magic-wavelength step rather than on accuracy records, which separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. Katori and Ye are the most defensible pair, though I would still want an archival check of the 2001-2003 priority record (Lemonde and others) and of what Ye's credit rests on. P002 keeps this part but adds a one-name IceCube credit for a very large collaboration that I cannot verify as the original work. P003 is a platform prize with a contested three-from-five allocation and a proposal credit that was shared. I rank both of those below P001 but above no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I have no documented link to Katori, Ye, RIKEN or JILA. Chalmers department-level affiliation with Goran Johansson (B038, not on this slate) is noted, and my exchanges with the Japanese microscopy community are not connected to the credited names.
